neighbours.label: a relative word right after a coordinator: the second conjunct of a relative clause ('and which', 'or that')
fire: This is a recipe my mother taught me and which I still make every winter.
She chose a route that avoids the hills and that passes two lakes.
It is a tool many carpenters own but which few of them use well.
We want parts that ship quickly or that can be made locally.
He wrote a book that sold poorly and that nobody reviewed.
These are rules we inherited and which no one has dared to change.
They need a venue that is cheap or that offers free parking.
The town has a law that dates from 1890 and which is still enforced.
quiet: This is a recipe my mother taught me, and I still make it every winter.
She chose a route that avoids the hills and passes two lakes.

predictions: 6/8 fire; a single relative clause with no coordinator stays quiet
notes: Card: ' is', ' ever', ' what', ' none', ' which', 'or that', 'and which', 'versus what'. Probe: 'and which' 0.35, 'or that' 0.45; plain 'and I' 0.01; 'versus what' 0.09, 'nor ever' 0.06, so only the relative-word case is claimed.
